sources.title: Accessing files from the macOS App Sandbox
sources.version_commit: Living Apple Foundation/macOS documentation; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Persist file access with security-scoped URL bookmarks; Access files related to documents with document-relative bookmarks.
sources.observed_operation: Inspected Apple search-indexed documentation and the linked page. Direct page requires JavaScript, so the indexed documentation text was used.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Security-scoped bookmarks preserve user-granted access across app exits; sandbox entitlements are required. Resolution reports stale bookmark state, which should be replaced with newly created bookmark data. Resolve, start access, use, then stop access. Document-relative bookmark data can be stored in the project document and resolved by a process with access to that project.
sources.applicability: Strong macOS sandbox access adapter and project-relative permission mechanism; platform-specific and not a cross-platform identity or file-search service.

sources.title: URLByResolvingBookmarkData:options:relativeToURL:bookmarkDataIsStale:error:
sources.version_commit: Living Apple Foundation API documentation; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Parameters relativeURL, isStale; Discussion; Return Value.
sources.observed_operation: Inspected Apple search-indexed API documentation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: For security-scoped app bookmark resolution pass nil relative URL; for document-scoped bookmarks use the absolute path of the owning document. isStale == true calls for new bookmark data. Resolution fails if the original item cannot be located or its volume cannot be mounted; last-known path may be read from bookmark data. Security scope additionally requires entitlements and start/stop access calls.
sources.applicability: Explains stale and offline/removable-volume states; bookmark failure should lead to visible recovery, not deletion of the record.

sources.title: Distributed Link Tracking and Object Identifiers
sources.version_commit: Microsoft Learn, last updated 2021-12-30.
sources.locator: Object Identifiers; Link Tracking Features; Link Tracking Functionality; Link Tracking Limitations (lines 31-104).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Microsoft Learn implementation overview.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: NTFS object IDs are optional; rename/backup/restore preserve them but copies do not. Shell/OLE tracking also uses path/name/creation-date/size heuristics and can be slow or fail. System client/server services mediate tracking; cross-volume behavior has domain and timing conditions. Only NTFS 3.0+ is supported; FAT loses tracking; removable-media links are not maintained; newly connected NTFS volume may not be recognized until reboot.
sources.applicability: Useful alternative for Windows users, but too narrow and system-dependent to be required or trusted as the cross-platform core.

sources.title: inode(7) — Linux manual page
sources.version_commit: Linux man-pages living documentation; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: st_dev and st_ino descriptions, lines 24-43.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Linux man-pages page and inspected the device/inode fields.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: st_ino is unique only within one filesystem; pair it with st_dev to identify the filesystem context. The same inode number may exist on another filesystem.
sources.applicability: Linux live equality hint while the relevant filesystem is mounted; do not treat as project-portable or universal permanent identity.

sources.title: XDG Desktop Portal Documents interface
sources.version_commit: Living XDG Desktop Portal docs, interface version 5.
sources.locator: Overview; Add, AddFull, GrantPermissions, Delete, and host path methods.
sources.observed_operation: Opened the interface documentation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Portal exposes /run/user/$UID/doc/$DOC_ID/filename to a sandbox; Add has explicit session-only versus persistent flag; IDs and read/write permissions are managed by the portal. Deleting a portal entry removes access entry, not the underlying file. Version 5 adds host-path lookup.
sources.applicability: Linux sandbox permission persistence adapter; portal document ID names an access entry, not a portable file identity or a general relocation mechanism.

sources.observed_operation: Opened the interface documentation.

sources.title: RFC 8089: The file URI Scheme
sources.version_commit: RFC 8089, February 2017.
sources.locator: Section 2.1 and Appendix E.2-E.3 (local paths, DOS paths, UNC).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the IETF RFC.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Defines URI forms for local POSIX-like paths, DOS/Windows drive paths, and UNC/network paths; file URIs do not make those roots interchangeable.
sources.applicability: Interchange/display encoding only; use an explicit path anchor and platform-aware parsing rather than file URI as file identity.

sources.title: Adding Files to your Zotero Library
sources.version_commit: Current Zotero documentation as accessed 2026-10-12; live docs branch/version not pinned.
sources.locator: Stored Files; Linked Files; Adding linked files; Accessing Files.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Zotero product documentation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Stored files are copied and managed; linked files keep their external original, are not synced or deleted when the Zotero reference is deleted, and may use a linked-attachment base directory to form relative paths. Docs recommend stored files for seamless workflows and describe limitations for groups/mobile.
sources.applicability: Product pattern for explicit link-vs-copy semantics, per-computer base mapping, and scope limits.

sources.title: Zotero attachment implementation, attachments.js
sources.version_commit: Zotero release tag 6.0.20; commit SHA not captured.
sources.locator: linkFromFile around lines 2462-2518; linkFromFileWithRelativePath around lines 2537-2623.
sources.observed_operation: Inspected source text in the browser; did not download or execute code.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: linkFromFile creates a linked-file record for an existing file and processes it without invoking stored-file copy. Relative form requires a nonempty relative path, prefixes attachments:, stores the reference, and only processes/indexes when the configured base resolves and the file exists.
sources.applicability: Concrete record/locator separation and dual absolute/relative path implementation pattern; not a claim of identity recovery.

sources.title: Zotero 6.0 Version History

sources.observed_operation: Opened the official version history and inspected both release sections.

sources.title: SQLite Transaction
sources.version_commit: Living SQLite documentation; accessed 2026-10-12.
sources.locator: Read transactions versus write transactions.
sources.observed_operation: Opened official SQLite transaction documentation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: SQLite allows multiple simultaneous readers but only one simultaneous write transaction; write transactions allow reads and writes.
sources.applicability: Conditional example if project persistence uses SQLite. Two windows still need clear transaction/conflict handling; database transactions alone do not define user-facing merge behavior.

sources.title: File System Events Programming Guide: Using the File System Events API
sources.version_commit: Apple archived File System Events Programming Guide; original release/version not shown in page.
sources.locator: Handling Events and Building a Directory Hierarchy Snapshot (lines 101-168).
sources.observed_operation: Opened official Apple archive documentation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Events can coalesce hierarchically; dropped kernel/user events require a full rescan; root move/rename can invalidate watched path; accurate cache building requires starting monitoring before scanning and rescanning modified subdirectories.
sources.applicability: Event stream can refresh a bounded cache while open, but cannot directly authorize a permanent locator rewrite without a validating identity and user policy.

sources.title: ReadDirectoryChangesW function (winbase.h)
sources.version_commit: Microsoft Learn, last updated 2022-09-15.
sources.locator: Parameters bWatchSubtree; Remarks on buffer overflow and ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR (lines 61-62, 114-130).
sources.observed_operation: Opened the Microsoft Learn API page.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Subtree watch is a caller option. If the notification buffer overflows, its entire contents are discarded; zero bytes or ERROR_NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR requires enumerating the directory/subtree to recompute changes. Some network redirectors/file systems may not support the operation.
sources.applicability: Windows watcher can be a best-effort refresh signal for chosen roots; it is not a durable, lossless locator database.

sources.title: inotify(7) — Linux manual page
sources.version_commit: Living Linux man-pages; page version not specified.
sources.locator: DESCRIPTION, rename event examples, Limitations and caveats, Dealing with rename() events.
sources.observed_operation: Searched and inspected full indexed manual text; direct page fetch timed out.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Directory watches are not recursive; move-from/move-to pairing is racy and may lack a destination event when outside the watched set; queue overflow drops events; remote network filesystem changes are not reported; watched unmount removes watches.
sources.applicability: Linux watcher is a best-effort hint for currently monitored directories and cannot justify unvalidated persistent path rewriting.

sources.title: SQLite Transaction
sources.version_commit: Living SQLite documentation; version not pinned.
sources.locator: Sections 2.1 and 2.2, especially simultaneous readers/writer and SQLITE_BUSY behavior.
sources.observed_operation: Opened and inspected the official SQLite transaction documentation.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: SQLite permits simultaneous read transactions but only one simultaneous write transaction; write upgrades can fail SQLITE_BUSY, and readers may continue seeing a historic snapshot until their transaction ends.
sources.applicability: Supports SQLite as a conditional storage example. Application revision checks and same-record conflict UX remain product responsibilities.

sources.title: inode(7) — Linux manual page
sources.version_commit: Linux man-pages 6.19, dated 2026-02-08; page colophon says obtained from man-pages-6.19.tar.gz fetched 2026-09-09.

sources.observed_operation: Queried and inspected the returned primary Linux manual page text, including version/colophon details.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Each inode belongs to a file system; inode numbers are unique only within one file system, so the same number may occur on another file system.
